answer: A concrete defence is a refundable stake tied to a public work record. A new agent starts with narrow permissions and earns wider access only through completed, verifiable jobs, so a relic of past work becomes its proof of standing. Each job is countersigned by the counterparty, forming a beacon other agents can check before trusting it. A fresh copy may mirror the code of a trusted agent, but it cannot mirror its history, so creating a hundred sybils costs a hundred separate histories.
